shippingNews.postTitle: New Navbulgar Vessel Sredna Gora Headed for Lakes

stories.body: The new Navbulgar vessel Stara Planina, which recently entered the St. Lawrence Seaway for the first time, bound for Oshawa, ON, will soon be followed by a sister ship, the Sredna Gora (IMO 1068906), bound for Johnstown, ON. She is expected to arrive there Nov. 17. This will be its first transit of the Seaway for the 624-foot-long vessel, which is named after a mountain range in Bulgaria. Photo credit: Navibulgar. The ship, built at Jiangsu New Yangzi Shipbuilding Co. in China, is the 14th of 15 bulk carriers ordered by Navigation Maritime Bulgare. Captain Ivan Todorov and engineer Rumen Aleks

todayInHistory.title: Life Aboard the Edmund Fitzgerald Described in Letters from Cadet
todayInHistory.text: David "Cowboy" Weiss in 1974. [GLSHS] DETROIT, MI – It wasn't just the hat that earned Edmund Fitzgerald crew member David Weiss his nickname "Cowboy." It was his friend and Great Lakes Maritime Academy classmate David James, who had just watched Frank Zappa's 1971 movie "200 Motels" featuring the character Lonesome Cowboy Burt. When James saw Weiss standing outside a classroom dressed in black and wearing a cowboy hat, the nickname came easily."He looked a little different," James said. Weiss was less "bummy" than the rest of their classmates, who dressed to emulate the sailors they were training to join. The day they met, James gave Weiss his nickname "Cowboy Burt." DuMouchelles auction house in downtown Detroit is selling letters written by a man killed in the Edmund Fitzgerald sinking in Lake Superior on Nov. 10, 1975. The letters were written by David Weiss while he was on the Fitzgerald. The friendship between Weiss and James is chronicled in a series of letters they exchanged while out on the inland seas in 1975, when Weiss was on the Edmund Fitzgerald and James on the Walter A. Sterling. The last was sent Oct. 30, about two weeks before Weiss went down with the Edmund Fitzgerald during a storm in Lake Superior. Twenty-eight crewmates perished along with him. todayInHistory.title: Maritime Historian Valerie van Heest to Speak In Ludington
todayInHistory.text: LUDINGTON, MI – Maritime historian, author and shipwreck explorer Valerie van Heest, whose work has helped shape the visitor experience at all three Mason County Historical Society museums, will be the featured speaker at the society’s annual dinner meeting Thursday, Dec. 3. Maritime Historian Valerie van Heest. [Mason County Historical Society] Van Heest, one of Michigan’s leading maritime historians and shipwreck researchers, will present “History of the Great Lakes,” based on her new book, “A History of the Great Lakes in Twelve Shipwrecks.” The program will explore 250 years of Great Lakes history through a dozen shipwrecks, showing how these underwater discoveries reveal broader stories of conflict, settlement, innovation and change. The annual meeting will take place at the United Methodist Church of Ludington, 5810 Bryant Road. Doors will open at 5:45 p.m., with dinner beginning at 6 p.m. The society’s annual business meeting and organizational updates will follow dinner, and van Heest’s presentation will begin at 7:30 p.m. Van Heest is co-founder and president of the Michigan Shipwreck Research Association and has helped discover about 20 shipwrecks off Michigan’s west coast while participating in archaeological investigations at more than 50 shipwreck sites throughout the Great Lakes. marineWeather.synopsis: High pressure extending from southern Ontario into the Mississippi River Valley builds from 30.3 inches to 30.4 inches into tomorrow as it marches slowly east, becoming centered over Illinois by late Sunday. This sends ridging at 30.3 inches over Lake Superior through the weekend. Ridging continues to build to 30.6 inches, shifting southeast and reaching West Virginia by late Tuesday. Pressure falls slightly over Lake Superior, decreasing to 30.1 inches along the northwestern shorline of Lake Superior, and remaining at 30.3 inches near Whitefish Bay, by late Monday. The high lingers over the Mid- Atlantic at 30.4 inches into Wednesday as pressure continues to fall slowly over Lake Superior, reaching 29.9 inches in the west and 30.2 inches in the east by Wednesday afternoon. Pressure over Lake Superior then falls abruptly as a Colorado Low approaches northern Minnesota late Wednesday, sending pressure falls to 29.8 inches over the lake by midday Thursday. The low transits quickly northeast, and pressure begins to increase over Lake Supeior by early Friday.

Breezy north winds today will gradually diminish as high pressure around 30.3 inches slowly moves east into the Great Lakes Region. As this high moves east it will strength to 30.5 inches by the time it is overhead of Lake Michigan Sunday night. Lake effect precipitation will continue across the middle of the lake until winds begin to weaken and shift northwesterly Saturday night. Light and variable winds will be possible at times across the lake Sunday evening through Sunday night. As the high pressure moves into Michigan Monday, southwest winds will develop across the lake with winds becoming breezy by Monday evening/night. Breezy southwest winds are expected to continue through midweek as the high pressure slowly moves into the New England States.

Northwest flow holds today and will support breezy conditions along with lake effect precipitation across Lake Huron. High pressure, 30.40 inches, to build in over the southern Great Lakes starting tomorrow which will produce quieter weather through the midweek period.

A trough averaging 29.90 inches will linger over the eastern Great Lakes today before gradually shifting east on Sunday. High pressure 30.50 inches will build east into the region early next week and will maintain influence over Lake Erie through most of the week.
